dispositions.justification: Retains the post-baseline workflow-guide update through the changed shared knowledge loader. Workflow groups remain informational human paths or unavailable capabilities, not new callable tools or execution authority.

Retains the post-baseline guide update and changed shared styling closure. Additional tables remain excluded from set_table_style; independent bindings, exact barcodes, source facts and human import and sharing boundaries remain documented.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. The UI cleanup does not expand global style keys, change the automatic-application allowlist, or bypass inspection and commit checks.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Exact field and label targets, closed patch schemas and protected bindings remain independent of SVG step rendering.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Original section targets, new identifier constraints and protected-binding checks remain; removing hidden suggestions grants no creation authority.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Existing-target and original protected-binding checks remain, while bound-field removal remains excluded from automatic application.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Reordering still requires the complete current identity set in an original section, and every draft step still enforces selected scope.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Original section targets and non-items grid restrictions remain closed; table header colors still belong to the separate table-style operation.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. The exact five-section permutation and repeating-header ordering requirement remain; the UI changes introduce no additional section targets.
Retains the post-baseline page-contract update. Supported media, custom dimensions and user-supplied printer constraints remain bounded, and page operations remain outside automatic application.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Logo changes still require an existing asset descriptor or null; shared UI SVGs provide no new asset or disclosure authority.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Collection changes remain restricted to available array bindings with protected-binding checks and remain excluded from automatic application.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Heading changes remain stored-text-only, cannot enable the header, and cannot expand heading-only selected scope.
Retains the post-baseline independent header-color update. The items-only closed patch still accepts six-digit hex or null, and selected-column authority does not permit whole-table styling.
Retains the post-baseline shared-contract update. Heading and page-number typography targets remain explicitly bounded and separate from table colors and presentation-only step icons.

Retains the post-baseline discovery-contract update. Capability retrieval reports granted tools and schemas without granting effects or independently establishing answer evidence; hidden-suggestion removal does not alter it.
Retains the post-baseline tool and guide updates. Reading a registered guide establishes evidence but grants no additional effects; retained step text is rendered as text rather than parsed HTML.

Retains the post-baseline context and shared-contract updates. Independent table colors remain exposed through authoring context, while retained step metadata remains excluded from subsequent provider history.

Retains the post-baseline typed-operation update. Private draft application still enforces scope and original protected bindings, and successful edits invalidate prior inspection and observation evidence.

Retains the post-baseline observation-contract update. Inspection still captures a candidate-bound receipt; SVG checks and visible completed steps do not replace the latest ready inspection required by finish.

Retains the post-baseline authorized-observation addition. Sharing remains explicit and single-use, with default-off controls under More settings; semantic observation still does not replace final draft inspection. Browser interaction is UNVERIFIED.

Retains the post-baseline scenario-tool addition. Synthetic scenario diagnostics still do not set the final inspection receipt, and changed step presentation grants no additional completion authority.

Retains the post-baseline shared-tool update. Successful private undo still invalidates inspection and observation evidence and clears the imported source handoff; visible activity remains presentation only.

Retains the post-baseline shared-tool update. Notes remain bounded and run-local; retained step labels are separate presentation metadata and are not projected into subsequent provider conversation context.

Retains the post-baseline completion-contract update. Finish still requires a latest ready inspection and current imported lineage for coding grants; source-bound proposals remain excluded from automatic application.

Retains the post-baseline answer-contract update. Exact answer text and latest-receipt checks remain intact; retained steps use safe text rendering and remain excluded from subsequent provider history.

Retains the post-baseline pixel-observation addition. Consent messages now name the existing More settings menu; text and pixel permissions remain separate, default-off and single-use. Browser execution is UNVERIFIED.

Retains the post-baseline blocker-contract update. Assistant-reported blockers still terminate without producing a proposal; clearer sharing instructions and SVG rendering do not suppress or reinterpret the blocker.
Retains the post-baseline source-workspace addition. Listing still requires genuine run-owned authorization; opening More settings or selecting observation sharing does not authorize source access.

Retains the post-baseline source-workspace addition. Bounded source reads still require separate fictional-source authorization; renamed settings and SVG icons do not authorize business values or host filesystem access.
Retains the post-baseline source-workspace addition. Search arguments remain bounded and handlers still require run-owned authorization; hidden-suggestion removal introduces no new paths or effects.

Retains the post-baseline source-workspace addition. Exact-digest replacement and null-digest creation remain explicit, source consent remains separate, and source-bound proposals still require human Apply.

Retains the post-baseline source-workspace addition. Atomic patch, creation and deletion contracts remain closed; UI step icons do not replace source authorization or the explicit human application boundary.

Retains the post-baseline source-workspace addition. The closed schema retains bounded execution arguments and empty-string root cwd semantics, with separate fictional-source consent. Runtime isolation is UNVERIFIED.

Retains the post-baseline source-workspace addition. Diff retrieval remains an authorized read against the original fictional starter; a visible successful step does not establish artifact acceptance or application approval.

Retains the post-baseline source-workspace addition. Artifact retrieval remains tied to successful current commands and host-bound descriptors; presentation changes do not bypass separate artifact import or completion checks.

Retains the post-baseline typed artifact-import addition. Imported operations still pass shared scope and protected-binding checks, invalidate inspection and retain source lineage; source-bound proposals cannot auto-apply.

Retains the post-baseline authoring-guide and table-color updates. Removing hidden suggestions and changing presentation icons do not alter typed operations, selected scope, protected bindings or final-inspection requirements.

Retains the post-baseline source-workspace guide addition. Separate single-run source consent, imported lineage, final inspection and explicit human Apply remain intact; cleanup failures still block new source work. Runtime behavior is UNVERIFIED.
